review: Independent image-by-image visual inspection of all six formal-release screenshots and supplied state JSON

desktop-closed.png.observation: Two different-height frosted bottles and fitted black pumps are entirely visible. Both labels retain liaose and OIL-INFUSED BODY CREAM. Page heading, four descriptions and controls are unobstructed.

desktop-half.png.observation: Both black pump assemblies rise together with their long clear tubes; bottles stay below. Two printing groups move farther left than the two transparent substrates. No viewport clipping.

desktop-open.png.observation: Two complete pump-and-tube assemblies, two empty bottles, two transparent label substrates and two complete printing groups remain visible with separation. Content does not collide with the heading or right descriptions.

desktop-rotated.png.observation: The roughly 90-degree view preserves two connected pump-and-tube assemblies and both bottles. Labels and printing become edge-on as expected; all groups remain within the viewport.

mobile-closed.png.observation: 393x852 simulated viewport: both bottles and complete pumps fit, title and four component controls remain readable, and bottom controls are visible. No model or text clipping.

mobile-open.png.observation: 393x852 simulated viewport: both raised pumps, thin transparent tubes, both bottles and separated print groups remain inside the width. Four component controls and full-open progress controls are visible.

limitations: Transparent tubes and label substrates have deliberately subtle contrast; visibility matches their clear material, and no structural break was observed.
Small package printing is not comfortably readable at the simulated mobile full-open scale; it remains visible as part of the complete print layer.
Mobile checks are viewport simulation, not physical-device or native-touch validation.
The screenshots and state files do not by themselves verify every server resource; HTTPS body/hash verification belongs to the publisher report.
